data.description:
## The defect

`rebar-gerrit-mirror-out-of-sync` pages on HEALTHY operation. It does not require replication to
be broken, or even slow — it requires one unlucky probe sample plus one ordinary scheduling gap.

Three compounding causes, all VERIFIED against live CloudWatch data:

**1. The publish cadence is not 5 minutes, but the alarm buckets at 5 minutes.**
`infra/scripts/observability.sh` §5 (line ~784 of 827) is the LAST section of the script, and the
script's wall-clock runtime varied 3-7 minutes tonight. So §5 publishes at run-start PLUS
script-runtime, which drifts against fixed 5-minute CloudWatch buckets. Measured: **6 of 47
five-minute buckets (13%) contain no datapoint at all** over ~4 hours.

Matched 1:1 by run (using `mcp_healthy`, published at line 131, as the run-start stamp):
```
run start (mcp) -> mirror published   lag
13:25            -> 13:28              3m
13:31            -> 13:34              3m
13:37            -> 13:43              6m
13:43            -> 13:50              7m
13:50            -> 13:53              3m
```
Exactly 1:1. No run was ever dropped.

**2. Every empty bucket is a free breaching datapoint.** `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`.

**3. `datapoints_to_alarm = 2` of `evaluation_periods = 3`.** So ONE real divergence reading plus
ONE scheduling gap pages. The 13:44:49 firing window was literally `1, MISSING, 1`.

## The alarm's own comment asserts this cannot happen. Both claims are false.

The Terraform comment states "the normal ~15s post-submit replication lag never pages" and
"~22 of 24 periods present is the observed norm". Measured reality: replication took up to
**2m44s** (bounded by a Mirror Guard run at 20:37:05 carrying the submitted sha), and periods
present is **87%, not 92%**. A comment asserting a safety property that measurement contradicts is
itself part of the defect — it is why nobody re-examined the tuning.

## Tonight's firing, fully reconstructed

Three Gerrit submits (authenticated REST timestamps, UTC):
```
2623  20:34:21 -> main bbe5d228
2630  20:43:38 -> main f58bbe58
2631  20:43:48 -> main 98d4ab96
```
Breaching datapoints at minute 20:34 and minute 20:43 — each inside the SAME MINUTE as a submit.

These were TWO INDEPENDENT sub-minute catches of fresh submits, not one nine-minute stuck
replication. Proof: a Mirror Guard run created 20:37:05 carried `head_sha = bbe5d228`, so GitHub
already had change 2623 by 20:37. For the probe to publish 1 in minute 20:43, its read must have
landed in the 22-second window AFTER submit 2630. `replication_errors` published 0.0 on every run
throughout.

Recovered at 13:50 PDT (0.0 at 13:50 and 13:53). The alarm nonetheless stayed in ALARM because
both post-recovery readings landed in the SAME 13:50 bucket, leaving 13:45 and 13:55 empty:
`MISSING, 0, MISSING`.

## Corroboration

The previous firing (2026-08-30) lasted exactly **6 minutes**, ALARM 10:36:30 -> OK 10:42:30. A
six-minute self-clearing page is the signature of this aliasing, not of a stuck mirror.

## Why this matters beyond noise

An alarm that fires on healthy operation trains its readers to skim past it. That is the same
signal-quality decay that made `sweep (windows)` worthless as a health signal — and it is
especially costly here, because this alarm guards a condition (mirror divergence) where CI would
be testing a different tree than Gerrit's main. When it eventually means something, nobody will
believe it.

## The design fault, stated precisely

The alarm treats "the probe did not happen to land in this bucket" as identical to "the mirror is
broken", while the metric's publisher has no cadence guarantee. The dead-publisher concern that
motivated `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` is LEGITIMATE and must not be discarded — a silently
dead publisher is exactly the inversion ticket `bff5` fixed across 11 alarms. The error is
conflating liveness and divergence in ONE metric with ONE window.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 - A single submit (or a batch of submits) followed by normal replication does NOT page.
      Demonstrate against the reconstructed timeline above: `1, MISSING, 1` must not alarm.
- [ ] AC2 - Dead-publisher detection is PRESERVED. If `observability.sh` stops running entirely,
      something still pages. Losing this to fix the noise would re-introduce the `bff5` inversion.
- [ ] AC3 - A genuine sustained divergence still pages, and within a defensible time. State the
      chosen bound and why.
- [ ] AC4 - The tuning is justified against MEASURED cadence, not assumed cadence. The current
      comment's "~22 of 24 periods" claim must be replaced with a measured figure and the
      measurement recorded, so the next reader can check it rather than trust it.
- [ ] AC5 - Defect-seeded: a test or documented check fails if the alarm is retuned back into a
      configuration where one scheduling gap plus one divergence sample pages.

## Candidate direction (not prescriptive)

A separate liveness alarm on a longer window would preserve the dead-publisher catch while letting
the divergence alarm stop treating scheduling jitter as evidence. Other options: publish §5 on its
own schedule rather than at the tail of a variable-length script; widen the divergence window;
require more datapoints. The AC set deliberately does not choose.

## Not a real problem tonight

The mirror is IN SYNC (verified directly: `gerrit/main` and `origin/main` both
`98d4ab96325dc679b0a3dd977a5af33a65f454a3`). No action needed beyond this ticket.
data.title: rebar-gerrit-mirror-out-of-sync pages on healthy operation: 13% of buckets are empty by cadence aliasing and treat_missing=breaching makes one gap plus one submit-sample enough to alarm
